turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, I guess the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be sitting there trying to work on a job application—which, by the way, those online portals they make you use now are the absolute worst. You upload your resume and then they make you type the exact same stuff into these little boxes anyway. It makes zero sense. My buddy Dave was complaining about the exact same thing when we were playing Xbox the other night. We usually play Call of Duty, but the new update totally ruined the matchmaking, so we were... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, so I'll be trying to do an application, and then a car drives by outside, or my phone lights up, or I just get some random idea in my head. Like suddenly I'm thinking about fixing the chain on my bike, and the next thing I know I'm out in the garage looking for a wrench, and I end up somewhere totally different before I even notice I stopped working on the application. It just keeps happening like that.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes an inability to sustain attention on tasks, such as trying to complete a job application but abandoning it to do something else without realizing it.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly states they are easily pulled off track by extraneous stimuli like sounds, their phone, or unrelated random thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with staying focused on tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Um, I'd say it’s been this bad... like, really disruptive, for about a year and ten months? Yeah, almost two years. It started getting this way right after my soccer injury. That completely knocked me out of my usual routine. 

I used to play in this Sunday league down at the rec center. We actually won the championship the year before, which was insane because our goalie was honestly the worst. Like, he would literally flinch and close his eyes when the ball came at his face. We had to rely entirely on our defense. But anyway, I went up for a header and came down totally wrong on my leg. The guy at the urgent care said it was a really nasty sprain and I had to wear this massive boot for weeks. It was super annoying trying to sleep with it, so I ended up just staying awake on the couch watching reruns of The Office. Have you ever noticed how the lighting in the first season is weirdly gray and depressing compared to the later ones? It's like they didn't figure out the cameras until season three. 

But, uh, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, so about a year and ten months, ever since that injury just completely wrecked my normal schedule.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient confirms the doctor's premise of having difficulty staying focused on tasks, stating it has been disruptive for a year and ten months.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about a soccer goalie and a TV show instead of directly answering the question.
symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient demonstrates difficulty concentrating by losing their train of thought and forgetting the doctor's question mid-response ('wait, what did you ask me?').

Do you also notice this same kind of difficulty staying on track in other areas of your life—like when you're with friends, at home relaxing, or doing other activities—or is it mainly when you're trying to do work-related tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it's definitely not just the job stuff. It happens with pretty much everything, even stuff I actually want to do. Like, I’ve been trying to fix up this old dirt bike I bought off Craigslist—the guy said it just needed a new carburetor, but honestly, I think the whole engine block is shot. He totally ripped me off, but whatever. Anyway, I'll try to watch a YouTube video on how to rebuild it, or I'll try to read the service manual, and I'll get maybe two or three minutes in before I realize I'm just staring blankly at the screen. I end up having to rewind the video like five times because absolutely none of it stuck in my head. 

It’s just like when I try to watch movies now. I tried watching that new sci-fi movie everyone is talking about, the one with the huge spaceships that look like giant floating rocks? The special effects are crazy good, but the plot makes zero sense. Like, why would aliens travel across the entire galaxy just to steal our water? They could literally just mine ice from comets. Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, other areas of my life. Yeah, it happens all the time. I just zone out and have to start over, whether it's reading a manual or watching a video or whatever.

It always gets stuck in your shoes and then you track it into the house, and my mom would lose her mind...

My buddy Dave actually threw a pen across the room once because I wouldn't stop clicking it while we were trying to figure out our fantasy football draft. Which, by the way, my team was an absolute disaster this year. I drafted this running back in the first round because all the analysts said he was gonna have a breakout season, right? But then his offensive line was basically made of Swiss cheese. I mean, the quarterback was running for his life on every single play. It's like they didn't even practice blocking during training camp. And don't even get me started on the coaching staff. We have this whole thing where the loser has to spend 24 hours in a Waffle House, but you can knock an hour off for every waffle you eat. I've been trying to figure out the math on it, like, is it better to just pace yourself and eat one an hour, or do you try to eat ten right away and make yourself sick? I feel like the syrup is what really gets you...

Wait, sorry, I totally lost track there. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the fidgeting thing. Yeah, I'm always messing with my hands or bouncing my leg. It's just really hard to sit completely still.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about fantasy football and loses track of the conversation.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient explicitly confirms bouncing his leg, clicking pens, and jingling keys without realizing it.

They were the bright neon green ones that all the pros were wearing at the World Cup. I spent way too much money on them, and I only got to wear them for like three games before they had to cut them off me in the emergency room. I was so mad about the cleats, I almost didn't even care about my knee at first. And the physical therapy was a nightmare. The therapist was this guy named Chad who made me do these resistance band exercises that felt like torture...

Wait, sorry. The timeline, right. Yeah, so it's been this disruptive for about a year and ten months. Before the injury, I had soccer and a whole routine that kind of kept me in check, but once that was gone, everything just completely fell apart.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned you were always fidgety and had trouble focusing back in middle and high school, but I want to understand this better. Well, right now I'm actually unemployed. I've been trying to get into this automotive technician program, because like I said, I'm really good with cars. Well, except for the go-kart thing, but real cars I understand. The hands-on stuff just makes sense to my brain. 

But trying to actually get into the program has been a nightmare. I keep missing the deadlines for the online training modules you have to do before they even let you near a shop. The website they use is so clunky, it looks like it was built in 1998. It has that weird gray background with the blue hyperlinks? And every time you click something, it opens in a new window instead of a new tab. I hate that. It clutters up my whole screen. I actually spent like two hours trying to find a browser extension that forces everything to open in a tab, but then I went down this rabbit hole reading reviews for different ad blockers, and by the time I looked at the clock, it was 3 AM. I ended up downloading this one that changes all the ads to pictures of cats, which is funny for about five minutes until you're trying to read a serious article and there's just a giant orange tabby staring at you. 

Anyway, because I keep getting distracted and missing the deadlines, I've had to redo the whole application process a couple of times. So yeah, I'm just kind of stuck right now, not really moving forward with the technician thing, even though I know I could do the actual work if they'd just let me in the garage.
